Coram: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA ------
For the Petitioner : Mr. R.S. Mazumdar, Sr. Advocate For the State : Mr. V.K. Vashistha, Spl.P.P For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. R.N. Chatterjee, Adv.
------
Order No.05 Dated- 19.08.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1961 of 2020 instituted under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

3. As per complaint, the allegation is that petitioner fraudulently purchased a portion of land area 0.75 decimal out of 1.50 acres of land bearing R.S. Khata No.41, R.S. Plot No.17 from one Md. Mobin who happens to be grandson of the complainant showing him as dead.

It is further alleged that petitioner after knowing the real facts about alive of the complainant, has purchased the said land in conspiracy with other co-accused persons with a view to cheat the complainant and deprived him from landed property.
4. Learned senior counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case with ulterior motive.

It is further submitted that petitioner has paid valuable consideration amount against the said land in question and he is bonafide purchaser having no knowledge about the said facts as made by the vendor at the time of execution of sale deed.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

5. Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submits that the petitioner and the complainant belongs to the same village and petitioner has full knowledge about the grandfather of Imtiyaz Khan vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97382376/
1 the vendor that he is still alive, despite that petitioner has fraudulently purchased the said landed property with a view to cheat the complainant.

sentences.text: Hence, petitioner may not be extended privilege of anticipatory bail.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record and also in view of the facts that only summons has been issued against the petitioner, hence, there is no requirement of custodial trial in this case, hence, I am inclined to extend privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender before the Court below within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned J.M., Dhanbad in connection with Complaint Case No. 1961 of 2020 and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Pappu/
